item.title: Bilal Coulibaly chases market value, eyes big summer free agency
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A new season begins with restricted free agency looming for France's Bilal Coulibaly

The post Bilal Coulibaly chases market value, eyes big summer free agency appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Bilal Coulibaly is now entering a pivotal contract year with the Washington Wizards. The young French wing will earn $9.2 million this season. This is the final year of the rookie deal he signed after the 2023 NBA Draft, presented by State Farm.

Coulibaly was one of 23 players eligible for a rookie scale extension this offseason. However, he did not reach an agreement with Washington before the deadline on Monday. Instead, he joined a group of 14 players across the league who are now playing out their current contracts. He shares this scenario with Anthony Black, Scoot Henderson, Noah Clowney, Dereck Lively II, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Brice Sensabaugh, and others.

As a result, the Paris native is on track to become a restricted free agent next summer. To maintain his matching rights, the Wizards must tender a qualifying offer worth $10.3 million. This mechanism allows them to match any outside offer sheet from rival teams.

Since coming to the NBA from Metropolitans 92 after sharing the floor with Victor Wembanyama during the 2022–23 season, Coulibaly has built a reputation as a reliable perimeter defender. Injuries shortened his first three seasons, but his development remains steady. He averaged 10.8 points per game over 178 career appearances, and started 56 games last season. He also won an Olympic silver medal with France in 2024.

Moving into the 2026–27 Regular Season, a strong performance this year would directly increase his market value before he hits free agency.

item.title: Knicks draft pick Jack Kayil sidelined with calf injury
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
An injury setback halts Jack Kayil's momentum just months after his NBA Draft selection

The post Knicks draft pick Jack Kayil sidelined with calf injury appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

ALBA Berlin point guard Jack Kayil will miss several weeks after sustaining a calf muscle injury. The Basketball Champions League outfit and reigning easyCredit BBL champions in Germany updated the youngster’s status on Monday.

The setback leaves head coach Pedro Calles without a key playmaker moving deeper into the 2026–27 schedule, while halting Kayil’s momentum just months after the 2026 NBA Draft, presented by State Farm. The New York Knicks secured his rights with the 39th overall pick in the second round.

Rather than moving to North America immediately, he chose to develop in Europe. Kayil had even bypassed a commitment to Gonzaga to keep his name in the draft pool. In early August, the 20-year-old Berlin native also tied his future to ALBA by signing a five-year contract.

He earned NBA interest through a stellar breakout run last season while on loan at the Albatrosse. He guided his hometown club to a Bundesliga title. He also claimed the Best Young Player award in both the domestic league and the BCL.

Losing him hurts a roster facing two very different campaigns. In continental play, his side leads Group G with a 2–0 record, boosted by the NBA prospect’s averages of 9.5 points, 7.5 assists, and 2.5 steals per contest. They want the top seed to secure a direct ticket to the Round of 16. Domestically, the team has stumbled to a 2–3 start after three consecutive losses, but advanced to the Quarterfinals of the BBL-Pokal shortly after Kayil was officially sidelined.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama brings Spurs where the journey began: “Surreal”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Inside the San Antonio Spurs’ visit to France ahead of the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season

The post Victor Wembanyama brings Spurs where the journey began: “Surreal” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The San Antonio Spurs are ready for a new chapter. After fighting their way to the NBA Finals 2026, they open the 2026–27 Regular Season this Tuesday. They host the Oklahoma City Thunder at the Frost Bank Center. But before tipping off the 82-game calendar, a new video posted Monday reveals how this roster truly came together over the summer.

The squad traveled to France. Led by Victor Wembanyama, the Spurs spent days exploring Paris. The documentary captures them adapting to French culture, sharing meals, and touring landmarks like the Louvre. They also put in hard offseason work. France became the backdrop for their team chemistry.

The most powerful moment of the trip happens inside a quiet gym on the outskirts of Paris. This is where Wemby grew up. “I would say because it’s two of my worlds meeting in one place, in one moment,” he described after team practice on Monday, reflecting on the latest experience in his childhood facility. “I’m in the exact same gym where I was when I was 15, and with these guys that I met when I was 19. And a place where I lived intense emotions with people whom I lived intense emotions with as well. These two things meeting. It’s surreal at times. It is a great experience.”

For the towering center, France represents his roots and his earliest NBA dreams. Bringing his teammates into that space created a lasting bond.

The video above offers a rare look at these players outside the pressure of the league, displaying a brotherhood built on French soil.

item.title: Fontecchio eyes NBA title alongside Giannis: “Go all the way”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Part of a strong international core around Giannis Antetokounmpo, Simone Fontecchio points to an NBA championship

The post Fontecchio eyes NBA title alongside Giannis: “Go all the way” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Italian forward Simone Fontecchio shared his thoughts on the Miami Heat’s NBA championship potential in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, posted Sunday. “When you acquire a generational talent like Giannis and add key veterans to the roster, your only goal is to go all the way,” he stated.

The native of Pescara noted that Giannis Antetokounmpo arrived early in Florida to fit in quickly, observing that ‘having several European teammates has also helped’ the Greek superstar find his footing within head coach Erik Spoelstra’s lineup. Alongside the Greek Freak, the team features a strong continental presence with Russian Vladislav Goldin, Serbian Nikola Jovic, and Swedish Pelle Larsson.

Reflecting on his place in the rotation, Fontecchio expressed confidence about keeping a steady role. “Our coach knows he can always count on me, and I have his trust, which is crucial for a player,” explained the 30-year-old forward.

After a Preseason 2026 stretch where he tallied 8.6 points, 1.8 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.2 blocks, and 0.2 steals over five appearances, he is set to start his fifth year in the league. The Heat open their 2026–27 Regular Season against the Minnesota Timberwolves at the Kaseya Center on Wednesday night.

From 77 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague appearances, Fontecchio opted to move to North America in 2022, five years after going undrafted. He has since appeared in 263 NBA fixtures, including a 70-game stint with Miami last season with 8.5 points per contest. Last July, he re-signed for a second season.

item.title: NBA elevates fan experience with digital enhancements for 2026–27 season
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Innovative upgrades for the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, providing fans with real-time access to live games

The post NBA elevates fan experience with digital enhancements for 2026–27 season appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The NBA announced new digital experiences to bring fans closer to live games starting with the 2026–27 Regular Season.

Additional details were shared on Monday.

Per the press release: “The National Basketball Association (NBA) today announced a range of new and enhanced digital experiences for the 2026-27 season designed to keep fans connected to live games in real time and make it easier to watch the action across the platforms they use every day.

The NBA is expanding Tap to Watch, creating more direct connections between the places fans discover and follow NBA content and where they can watch games live. This season, Tap to Watch links will appear on every TikTok post mentioning #NBA, as well as on content from hundreds of creators who have been granted access to NBA game highlights this season. In both cases, fans get easy access to live games directly from the content they’re already engaging with.

The new NBA Gametime experience on X will also help fans discover where to watch live games alongside real-time scores, highlights and conversations in a custom NBA timeline. Tap to Watch will continue to connect fans to national, local, international and NBA League Pass game telecasts through the NBA App, NBA.com, team digital platforms and participating partner sites, including Google, which will again feature Tap to Watch links in OneBox search results and on its new Sportscaster platform. Fans can also now add the NBA schedule to their digital calendars via nba.com/calendar, with Tap to Watch links that take them directly to where each game is available.

Across the NBA App, NBA.com and social platforms, the league is introducing new ways for fans to discover what is happening across the league, follow games as they unfold and quickly access live broadcasts. The updates are highlighted by “Game Pulse,” a new NBA App experience that brings together real-time highlights, stats and insights to capture the story of the game as it happens, as well as AskNBA, an AI-powered basketball assistant that uses new in-game advanced stats and analysis to let fans dive deeper into the game through questions about games, players, statistics and on-court trends, backed by official NBA data.

Game Pulse combines a live court visualization with highlights, player and team milestones and advanced statistics, including shot charts and quarter-by-quarter player stats, in a live-updating experience. Fans can follow live or catch up quickly with contextual insights on momentum-shifting plays and individual performances. Throughout the season, Game Pulse will also feature commentary and perspectives from NBA legends such as Muggsy Bogues, Carlos Boozer, Gary Payton and Joakim Noah as well as creators, including Lethal Shooter, Kris London, Jenna Bandy and more.

Fans can also begin following the action before tipoff with live warm-up coverage available daily on the NBA App, providing a real-time look at players preparing for that night’s games and another way for fans to stay connected to the action.

“The breadth of our digital ecosystem allows us to connect with NBA fans in more ways than ever before,” said NBA Head of Direct to Consumer Products, Technology & Operations Chris Benyarko. “This season, we’re bringing together new experiences, deeper basketball insights and fresh perspectives from creators, while making it easier for fans to discover, follow and watch live games across the platforms they use every day. Together, these enhancements are designed to bring fans closer to the game and create a richer, more engaging experience throughout the season.”

Additional new and enhanced features across the NBA’s digital ecosystem this season include:

NBA Inside the Game powered by AWS: The league will combine tracking data with AI to provide fans with robust statistical insights around previously unmeasurable aspects of the game in real time, including new advanced stats such as Handle Score, which captures the style and effectiveness of every dribble move, and a new zone defense model showing how often and successful teams are at using it. NBA Blueprint leverages AI to produce pregame and postgame reports for every game, giving fans a quick read on each matchup’s biggest statistical advantages and storylines, with insights also appearing within Game Pulse.

NBA League Pass and AI-Assisted Navigation: NBA League Pass will debut several enhancements to the live game-viewing experience. Auto-Play Next will direct users to a recommended matchup at the conclusion of each game, while Multiview Focus Mode will allow fans to highlight a primary game while watching up to three additional matchups. Fans can also access a personalized Multiview card featuring four games based on the teams they follow in the NBA App. New AI-assisted navigation on the NBA App will also make it easier for fans to access information including scores, schedules and standings.”

item.title: Domantas Sabonis opens up on referee talks: “Sometimes it works”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Cleared 100% for the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, 30-year-old Domantas Sabonis is determined to bounce back

The post Domantas Sabonis opens up on referee talks: “Sometimes it works” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The Sacramento Kings are ramping up for the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, and a healthy Domantas Sabonis is central to their plans. The Lithuanian forward-center is entering his 11th year in the league. He wants to bounce back after injuries limited him to just 19 appearances last year.

To ensure he was ready, Sacramento took a cautious approach during the Preseason 2026. The Portland native played only the opening and final games of the schedule, averaging 9.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 2.0 steals per contest. “We were just taking it slow,” he explained after team practice on Sunday. “I was getting in my work, and the plan was to play the first one, finish on the last one.”

Getting back into game shape presented unique challenges after the extended layoff. “It’s definitely more difficult than one would expect,” Sabonis admitted. “You’re obviously healthy, cleared 100%, and then once you get out there playing NBA live, there’s obviously little bumps and bruises that come up. Your body hasn’t been used to getting pushed or working at that load for eight full months.”

“I talk to refs”

Sabonis is also managing his physical style with game officials. Discussing his legal screens, he revealed how he keeps communication open. “I talk to the refs,” he noted. “I’m like, ‘I’ve been doing this for so many years, you know how I set screens, I’m doing them legal’.”

“Depending on the player, he’s going to flop or not,” continued the veteran big. “I’m just going to set it more strong, more solid.”

The officiating crews understand his reputation. “They’re like, ‘OK, we know Sabonis, so we’ll see’. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t,” he smiled.

The Kings now get a real test. They open their 2026–27 journey against the Los Angeles Clippers at the Intuit Dome on Wednesday. They then host the Portland Trail Blazers at Golden 1 Center on Friday.

item.title: Doncic refuses to predict Lakers chemistry timeline, defers on leadership style
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
The Los Angeles Lakers and Luka Doncic face a learning curve to start the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season

The post Doncic refuses to predict Lakers chemistry timeline, defers on leadership style appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Following the NBA Preseason 2026, the Los Angeles Lakers are shifting focus to the 2026–27 Regular Season. Luka Doncic talked about team chemistry, health, and his role on a revamped roster after Monday’s practice.

Asked if his leadership style has changed since his early days in Madrid or his time in Dallas, the 27-year-old guard deferred to his teammates. “I think that’s the question for other people, how this team sees a leader,” he underlined. “I’m just my own leader. Like I’ve said, I’ve been in these situations a lot, but I think I’m doing a great job with this group.”

The squad faces a steep learning curve, natural growing pains. Key starters are still learning how to play together. When pressed on how much patience the group will need early on, Doncic kept a practical outlook. “I don’t know how much patience is going to be needed,” he admitted. “Just the start of a new season, a lot of new guys, but I can’t see in the future, so I don’t know how much patience we’re going to need.”

An injury cut his previous year short. However, the Slovenian superstar confirmed he is healthy and ready for a fresh chapter. He brushed off any extra pressure, focusing strictly on the game itself. “Excited to start playing,” he calmly replied. “Nothing new, I’m always very excited.”

Starting an 82-game marathon, the Lakers open the new season Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors at crypto.com Arena.

item.title: Wemby skips coasters but looks for championship with Spurs: “We’re ready”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Inspired by more experienced NBA stars, 22-year-old Victor Wembanyama is ready to begin the 2026–27 Regular Season

The post Wemby skips coasters but looks for championship with Spurs: “We’re ready” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

French superstar Victor Wembanyama enters his fourth NBA season as the Most Valuable Player betting favorite. His San Antonio Spurs open the 2026–27 Regular Season on Tuesday by hosting the Oklahoma City Thunder in Frost Bank Center. Reflecting on the physical toll of deep postseason runs, following the NBA Finals 2026 appearance, he praised the league’s top talents.

“I wonder how these guys do it for 10, 15 years. I guess you build up the kind of resistance that’s needed for that over the years with maturity,” the 22-year-old center said, expressing his awe. “I see it almost every day with guys like Shai, Giannis, Jokic, these guys.”

Wemby also shared a lighter moment from a weekend team trip to Six Flags, where his height ironically became an issue. “I can’t do it safely, so I’d rather not do it,” he joked. “I didn’t pass the height requirement.” Looking ahead to the grueling calendar, he confirmed his team is energized. “Last season just ended,” he noted, maintaining his humorous approach before completing his answer in a more serious tone. “We’ve had the time to settle down and retrain and get excited again for this. So, we’re ready.”

Bona questionable, Porzingis out

Beyond France’s premier talent, several European players shape the opening-night medical reports. The visiting Thunder will lack Serbian Nikola Topic due to low back surgery. With the New York Knicks raising their championship banner, the Philadelphia 76ers travel to face them without German Ariel Hukporti, who tore his right Achilles tendon. The Sixers also listed Turkish Adem Bona as questionable with a left foot sprain.

The Spurs will play without Tobias Harris due to a left calf strain, while teammate Jayden Quaintance recovers from knee surgery. The Thunder are also missing Otega Oweh and Thomas Sorber for surgical rehabilitation as well. For Philadelphia, Dominick Barlow is out for at least two weeks with a back issue, while Tacko Fall is out with a groin strain. Furthermore, the 76ers also consider Anfernee Simons and Dean Wade as questionable, while the Boston Celtics ruled out Devin Carter due to illness for the clash with the Detroit Pistons in Little Caesars Arena.

In a health update regarding Wednesday’s openers, Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr expects Stephen Curry to play against the Los Angeles Lakers. The star guard cleared a major hurdle by participating in a full practice on Monday ahead of the matchup at crypto.com Arena. However, Latvian Kristaps Porzingis remains sidelined.

item.title: Brandon Miller agrees to five-year, $209 million Hornets extension
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic

Charlotte secured the forward’s long-term future as he prepares for a bigger role following LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges’ departures

The post Brandon Miller agrees to five-year, $209 million Hornets extension appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

Brandon Miller agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale extension with the Charlotte Hornets, his representatives told ESPN’s Shams Charania.

The No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft averaged a career-best 20.2 points, along with 4.9 rebounds, while shooting 38.3% from three across 65 games last season. Charlotte went 41-24 with him available and 3-14 without him, ultimately losing in the second play-in game.

Miller underwent shoulder surgery in May but has fully recovered and played in preseason. Entering his fourth NBA season, he is expected to take on greater responsibility after the Hornets traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges.

item.title: Lakers waive Dalton Knecht, Bucks part ways with Kevin Porter Jr.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic
item.description:
Both teams cleared roster spots ahead of the NBA season, with former PAOK guard Porter joining Knecht on waivers

The post Lakers waive Dalton Knecht, Bucks part ways with Kevin Porter Jr. appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

The Los Angeles Lakers waived Dalton Knecht ahead of the NBA’s roster deadline, while the Milwaukee Bucks also released Kevin Porter Jr. to finalize their squad for the upcoming season.

Knecht’s departure, reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania, ended his two-season stint with the Lakers. The No. 17 pick in the 2024 draft averaged 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds as a rookie but struggled in his second season. Los Angeles reportedly explored a trade before opting to waive him.

The Lakers had previously agreed to send Knecht to Charlotte in the 2025 trade for Mark Williams, but the deal was rescinded after Williams failed his physical.

Porter, who played for PAOK in 2024 before returning to the NBA, was released as Milwaukee reduced its perimeter options. Injuries limited him to 38 appearances last season, though he averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals.

The former PAOK guard joined the Bucks from the Los Angeles Clippers in February 2025. He underwent right knee surgery in April 2026, ending his regular season early.

item.title: EuroLeague CEO Chus Bueno on NBA Europe deal: “The telephone lines are open”
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic
item.description:
Chus Bueno warned against a divided European basketball market but said the league remained willing to discuss a deal

The post EuroLeague CEO Chus Bueno on NBA Europe deal: “The telephone lines are open” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

EuroLeague CEO Chus Bueno said discussions with the NBA remained possible despite club owners rejecting a collaboration proposal at their October 6 meeting at Lake Como.

With the NBA planning to launch a European league in 2027, Bueno told Reuters that any agreement would need to protect EuroLeague’s interests.

“We had some conversations after Como. And the position of the owners was very clear. We will always be open to listen, and to talk with the NBA about any potential deal. But it has to make sense for us,” Bueno said.

He declined to disclose the proposal’s terms but left the door open to a different arrangement.

“The telephone lines are open and, if something has not worked, maybe there’s something that can work in the future.”

Bueno warned that competing leagues would divide the market and undermine its value.

“If they decide to (enter into the market), it’s going to be a disaster. And they know, we know, and we ​don’t want that. If you are divided, you lose value, and then some third party benefits. One of the things that we don’t want is more fragmentation.”

EuroLeague is pursuing its own expansion to 24 teams, with up to eight long-term franchise licences and an announcement of new participants expected in mid-November. Bueno said the strategy should improve clubs’ finances, with only 40% of current licence holders financially sustainable.

“I think that in five years with this expansion, we could be in a position where most, if not all, of them will be (financially) sustainable.”

All 13 shareholder clubs have signed 10-year franchise agreements linked to that plan. Bueno considers departures unlikely and pointed to the financial consequences of leaving.

“If they want to leave, they have a penalty they can pay, and then the clubs can also ask for individual damages. They will lose the €80 million-plus that they have in shares.”

Returning would carry an additional cost.

“But if they ever want to come back, they will have to pay whatever number it is when they ask to come back.”

The post EuroLeague CEO Chus Bueno on NBA Europe deal: “The telephone lines are open” appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Fournier on NBA Europe and the danger of losing “the craziness of European basketball”
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic
item.description:
The Olympiacos guard discussed tensions with Panathinaikos, his relationship with Giorgos Bartzokas and his reservations about NBA Europe

The post Fournier on NBA Europe and the danger of losing “the craziness of European basketball” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

Evan Fournier addressed Tyler Dorsey’s social media outburst and the intensity of Olympiacos’ rivalry with Panathinaikos during an appearance on Magenta TV’s “Pick n’ Roll” show and also explained why he remains unconvinced by the prospect of NBA Europe.

Fournier believes that European basketball needs a better financial model, but questioned whether NBA involvement would preserve the atmosphere that makes it distinctive.

“I think Europe needs a better business model. At the same time, the atmosphere is incredible. If the NBA comes, it will want to change certain things. If you lose that, you will lose the craziness of European basketball. They’ll look at what works best from a business perspective, with teams in attractive cities like London, Manchester and Rome. Personally, I don’t see it.”

The French guard also reflected on his decision to stay with Olympiacos through 2028 and praised head coach Giorgos Bartzokas, while also supporting his teammate, Tyler Dorsey, who is currently out of the team because of comments he made on social media.

The Dorsey case

Dorsey’s public comments while Olympiacos was in Spain caught Fournier by surprise. He believes the matter should have stayed within the team.

“Yes, it was a surprise. Nothing had been said before. It’s certainly not a good idea to say those things on social media. These things should be handled privately. He knows that, for sure. I’m sure he regretted it. I’m not sure what will happen, though. The team needs to move forward and maintain a strong bond. We can’t let anything stop us from moving forward.”

Fournier’s feelings about the rivalry with Panathinaikos have changed since he arrived in Greece. While he values the passion surrounding the games, he believes some of the hostility damages the sport.

Asked whether a truce between the clubs was possible, he admitted he was less optimistic than during his first season.

“Honestly, I don’t think so. In my first year, I thought it was possible. But I saw that what was happening wasn’t very healthy. Players and fans usually follow the leadership. When the leadership shows that it wants to go to war, everyone else follows. I think it’s great that Greece has rivalries like this, but sometimes the boundaries are crossed.”

He pointed to online disputes and the absence of supporters at the Super Cup as examples of what needs to change.

“The battles on social media hurt the product. For example, I was very disappointed that there were no fans in the stands at the Super Cup with Olympiacos, Panathinaikos, PAOK and AEK. Everyone needs to take the first step. I’m not saying they have to love each other, but they should at least tolerate each other.”

That rivalry also affects his plans to spend time with fellow French players in Athens, including former Olympiacos center Moustapha Fall, now at Panathinaikos.

“We’ve spoken with Fall. I’m not sure this is the right time to do it. Maybe in the summer. Right now, it’s red against green. I love them, but during the season, I don’t think it’s the right time. With AEK, though, there’s a truce. I spoke with Thomas Heurtel today.”

Olympiacos as his final stop

Fournier was also asked about reported interest from the San Antonio Spurs before he extended his Olympiacos contract. He said any such discussions would have been handled by his agent.

“I have no idea. My agent handles those things. I told him this would be my last stop. I don’t know whether that report is true.”

His relationship with Bartzokas has helped him feel settled. Fournier praised the coach’s commitment and dismissed concerns about his emotional reactions.

“He genuinely cares. He has a gift. He cares about his players. Coaching is a very stressful job. His reactions aren’t a problem. The coach makes the decisions. He loves the team and Olympiacos. He’s excellent, honestly. We have a connection. I’m happy.”

The involvement of owners Panagiotis and Giorgos Angelopoulos has also stood out, particularly compared with his NBA experiences.

“In the NBA, you barely have a relationship with the owners. The difference is huge. You see them once or twice a year. I don’t know how it works at other European teams, but here they’re always present. They trust the coach, management and players, and they give us freedom. They’ve invited me to their homes. I went to Giorgos’ house in Mykonos, and I also had a meal with Panagiotis there.”

Looking back on a difficult opening season, Fournier said the team’s belief never disappeared.

“First of all, I started the season with an injury. There are ups and downs during a season. We never lost belief. The important thing is to work together to achieve our goals. In the end, everything finished perfectly.”

Winning the EuroLeague, however, did not compensate for the gold medal that has eluded him with France.

“No, it wasn’t redemption. It was something completely different. It’s a new chapter with Olympiacos. I’m enjoying it.”

Family, perspective and life in Greece

A video message from his father, François, prompted an emotional reflection on his upbringing and career. Fournier recalled how deeply competition was embedded in his family, including a childhood judo defeat.

“My parents were always competitive. When I lost a match, another parent came over to comfort me, but my father said: ‘No, winning matters.’ My parents show that they’re proud of me. My father hadn’t said it to me. Only my mother had.”

He also explained why he considers himself fortunate, despite occasions when he felt misunderstood by coaches.

“Sometimes coaches didn’t understand who I was or my competitive spirit. I was lucky to grow up in this family. They gave me everything. I grew up in Paris, where there’s a lot of competition. For many reasons, I feel very fortunate. As an athlete, you’re always looking ahead and forget what you’ve achieved. You have to make your own luck, but I’m definitely lucky.”

The interview ended on a lighter note: Fournier chose Paros over Mykonos, chicken gyros over pork and profiteroles over galaktoboureko.

“For some reason, everyone in Greece is trying to feed me. That’s something I’ll have to watch towards the end of my career”.

The post Fournier on NBA Europe and the danger of losing “the craziness of European basketball” appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Yabusele compares Panathinaikos to Celtics, backs EuroLeague – NBA cooperation
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic
item.description:
The French big man discussed his move to Panathinaikos, his NBA experiences and what NBA Europe could bring to the sport

The post Yabusele compares Panathinaikos to Celtics, backs EuroLeague – NBA cooperation appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

Guerschon Yabusele sees a connection between Panathinaikos and the Boston Celtics that goes beyond their shared colors.

Speaking on Magenta TV’s “Pick n’ Roll” show, the French big man discussed the similarities between the clubs and explained why he wanted to join Zeljko Obradovic’s team.

“I wanted to play for the best coach in the EuroLeague and alongside some of the best players. I wanted to join a top-level team that wants to be at the very top.”

Having experienced both European and NBA basketball, Yabusele acknowledged that direct comparisons are difficult. Still, Boston stood out when asked which NBA club reminded him of a European team.

“It’s difficult to make a comparison, but I’d say the Celtics and Panathinaikos because of the culture, the colors, and Boston’s Irish heritage. Still, Europe and the NBA are different.”

Boston was one stop on a journey that also took him to China, Philadelphia, New York and Chicago. Looking back, Yabusele said he could not have anticipated the path his career would take.

“I never imagined my career would turn out this way. I played in China, Philadelphia, Chicago, and New York. I try to stay grounded. As long as my family is doing well, I’m doing well.”

The different arenas and fan bases left their own impressions, including the support he experienced during difficult stretches.

“It’s been an incredible experience: different teams, different fans. Playing at Madison Square Garden was amazing. Going to TD Garden is a special experience. Playing in Philadelphia was incredible, too. The fans showed us love even when we were losing. My last stop, Chicago, was a different organization, but the fans were always there.”

The conversation also turned to NBA Europe. Yabusele welcomed the prospect of greater exposure and financial opportunities, extending beyond the players themselves.

“Personally, I think it could be a good thing. The NBA is the biggest market in sports, so why not use that exposure to grow, especially for the players? If it means more money for players, coaches, assistants and medical staff, why not?”

He pointed to London as an example of the cities that could benefit, while expressing a preference for cooperation between the NBA and the EuroLeague.

“If it can bring that exposure to places like London, one of the best cities in Europe, that would be great. I hope it goes well, but I want the EuroLeague and the NBA to work together. That would be very good for basketball in Europe.”

The post Yabusele compares Panathinaikos to Celtics, backs EuroLeague – NBA cooperation appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Olympiacos announces dismissal of complaint filed by Giannakopoulos’ daughter
item.dc:creator: Nikola Miloradovic
item.description:
The club announced that the complaint against vice president Giorgos Skindilias had been deemed unfounded and shelved

The post Olympiacos announces dismissal of complaint filed by Giannakopoulos’ daughter appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

Olympiacos announced on Monday that a criminal complaint filed by Despina Giannakopoulou, daughter of Panathinaikos owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos, against its vice president Giorgos Skindilias had been deemed unfounded and definitively shelved.

The complaint stemmed from events surrounding Game 2 of the Greek league finals at the Peace and Friendship Stadium in June 2025. According to Olympiacos, it led to Skindilias being arrested and taken to a police station while recovering from surgery.

The club also stated that a separate case concerning Dimitris Giannakopoulos’ conduct had been referred to the competent court. At the time of the incidents, Giannakopoulos had disputed allegations against him and announced legal action of his own, alleging defamatory statements and abusive chants targeting his daughter.

Olympiacos concluded its latest statement with criticism of social media activity, saying that its management preferred to turn to the Greek justice system and await its decisions.

Olympiacos’ statement in full:

“In June 2025, we all witnessed Dimitris Giannakopoulos’ inconceivable behavior during his visit to the Peace and Friendship Stadium for Game 2 of the playoff finals.

His hurried departure under escort was followed by the filing of spurious criminal complaints, with the perpetrators posing as victims. One such complaint was filed by his daughter, Despina Giannakopoulou, against Olympiacos BC vice president Giorgos Skindilias. She even demanded that the expedited arrest procedure be followed, leading to his arrest and being taken to a police station while he was recovering from surgery.

We issued a statement at the time saying: ‘Neither Olympiacos BC nor its presidents threaten children with sexual acts or put them up to filing false criminal complaints.’ Vindication was not long in coming. Despina Giannakopoulou’s complaint was deemed unfounded and definitively shelved. As for Dimitris Giannakopoulos’ actions, those have been referred to the competent court for judgment.

While others live on social media, seeking likes and followers, Olympiacos BC and its management prefer to turn to the impartial Greek justice system and await its judgment.”

Panathinaikos reacted with the following press release on the issue: “Despina Giannakopoulou filed a complaint against the representatives of Olympiacos BC regarding the vile chants directed at her last summer. She was, in fact, fully vindicated regarding all the sickening abuse she endured.

The presiding prosecutor accepted as fact both the utterance of the despicable chants against her and the fact that, the very next day, Olympiacos BC officially reposted them on its own official channels!

The prosecutor noted that he found no intent to defame on the part of Olympiacos BC itself regarding the posting of the video; consequently, he initiated legal proceedings against the actual individuals responsible for the chants.

Instead of feeling shame for these actions—which the prosecutor describes in detail—and instead of offering an apology after all these months, Olympiacos BC has—true to its usual form—issued inaccurate, ridiculous statements that insult the intelligence of anyone with even a basic level of common sense.

We didn’t expect anything better. That’s just who they are…”

The post Olympiacos announces dismissal of complaint filed by Giannakopoulos’ daughter appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Dallas Mavericks waive Dwight Powell

Dallas parted ways with its longest-serving player ahead of the regular season

item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

The Dallas Mavericks are waiving veteran center Dwight Powell, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported, ending his 12-year stint with the franchise.

The 35-year-old was on a non-guaranteed contract as Dallas finalized its roster ahead of the regular season. His departure closes a chapter spanning the Mavericks’ eras with Dirk Nowitzki, Luka Doncic and Cooper Flagg.

Head coach Dusty May had praised Powell’s contribution during preseason, highlighting his leadership and the team’s effectiveness with him on the floor. However, May stressed that roster decisions rested with president Masai Ujiri and general manager Mike Schmitz.

Powell appeared in both preseason games against Houston during the NBA China Games, averaging two points and three rebounds. Beyond those numbers, his physicality and screen setting had continued to earn praise as Dallas weighed its final roster decisions.

item.title: Dwight Howard quietly ends playing career following brief stint in Georgia
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
After two games in Georgia, 40-year-old Dwight Howard calls it a day

The post Dwight Howard quietly ends playing career following brief stint in Georgia appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Former NBA superstar and Hall of Famer Dwight Howard played the final game of his professional career on Saturday.

According to his team in Georgia, Black Fortress Tbilisi, the veteran center has officially retired. The announcement marks the end of an incredible, globetrotting journey. The Atlanta native’s final chapter concluded after two appearances in the Georgian Superliga.

In his debut against Iverioni Gori, he made an instant impact. He recorded 12 points, seven rebounds, and three blocks in just 17 minutes. Despite his efficient play, Black Fortress lost a close 75–70 battle. He took the floor one last time against Tbilisi State University, TSU. He logged 19 minutes, finishing with ten points, four rebounds, and two blocks. Black Fortress fell to 0–3 in the 2026–27 Regular Season after an 89–82 defeat.

Before heading overseas, Howard built a legacy as a dominant NBA force. Selected with the first overall draft pick in 2004, he powered up the Orlando Magic for eight years, carrying them to the NBA Finals in 2009. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year eventually won a championship with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020. Representing the United States in FIBA tournaments, he captured gold in the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games and bronze in the FIBA World Championship 2006.

After 18 years in the NBA, Howard chose a global path. He starred for the Taoyuan Leopards in Taiwan, and suited up in the Philippines and Mongolia. From there to his brief stint in Georgia.

item.title: Euroleague highlights Lake Como summit in video recap release
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Inside the key meeting of the Euroleague Commercial Assets Shareholder Clubs at Lake Como

The post Euroleague highlights Lake Como summit in video recap release appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The Euroleague Commercial Assets Shareholder Clubs recently met for a two-day session at Lake Como to map out a shared vision.

Organizers chose the location intentionally, explained chief executive officer Chus Bueno, noting that major decisions should happen in a setting known for historic events.

A central theme of the summit was solidarity.

To experience the energy firsthand, watch the full recap video above. Hear directly from the executives and club owners as they shape the future.

“The EuroLeague has a great identity,” noted LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne’s Tony Parker.

Executives emphasized that the EuroLeague relies on teams working together and deciding their common interests as a single unit. “It’s a real milestone for the future,” said Olympiacos’ Giorgos Angelopoulos.

With growth prioritized as the main objective, club owners pledged to exchange information and learn from each other’s examples, acknowledging that the entire league rises together because they are all in the same boat, as stressed by Panathinaikos Aktor’s Dimitris Giannakopoulos.

The collective ambition remains highly competitive on a global scale. As underlined by FC Bayern Munich’s Herbert Hainer, the goal is to expand this presence so that whenever fans around the world think of the sport, they think first of the EuroLeague.

At the ECA meeting on October 6, they reached a key strategic agreement to transform existing teams into franchises while simultaneously expanding the total number of franchises in the league. By leaving Lake Como aligned and committed, leadership has laid down a foundation to build a stronger future.

item.title: Three Potential Sleeper Teams Who Could Upset the EuroLeague Next Season
item.dc:creator: Antigoni Zachari
item.description:
Some underdogs are flying under the radar as they prepare to mount their own assault on the summit. 

The post Three Potential Sleeper Teams Who Could Upset the EuroLeague Next Season appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Eurohoops team / info@eurohoops.net

Athens’ Telekom Center had thousands of people crammed inside for last season’s EuroLeague final between Olympiacos and Real Madrid, and by the fourth quarter, most of the partisan Greek crowd in attendance weren’t really watching a basketball game anymore — they were watching thirteen years of hurt finally come to an end. The Thrylos had been to the Finals three times since their most recent triumph back in 2013, and on each occasion, they had left empty-handed. 

This time, though, the Reds arrived at their own Final Four as the best team in Europe by the numbers, a 26-12 regular season that made them the top seed, with Sasha Vezenkov — back home after chasing this exact outcome since his return in 2024 — collecting the season MVP award. They swept Monaco, then met Fenerbahçe in the semifinal and dismantled them, 79-61, inside the Telekom Center. 

Olympiacos’ Lengthy Drought Finally Comes to an End

Nobody in Athens needed reminding what a Real Madrid final meant. Los Blancos came out throwing haymakers, Trey Lyles scoring 21 of his eventual 24 points before halftime, and for a stretch, it looked like history was going to repeat itself in the cruelest way. But this time, Olympiacos wouldn’t let the same heartbreaking fate befall them. Ten lead changes. Five ties. The scoreboard read 80-80 with two minutes left before Evan Fournier and Alec Peters closed it out at the free-throw line, 92-85, and Georgios Bartzokas — the same coach who’d delivered the club’s last title back in 2013 — was lifted onto his players’ shoulders. 

What happens next tells you almost as much as the final itself. Bartzokas got extended through 2029 within weeks, and the roster since has barely moved. When you’ve just built the best team in Europe, it’s all about continuity, and it’s a tactic that online betting sites seem to agree with. 

The latest basketball odds at https://thunderpick.io/sports/basketball make Olympiacos a 3/1 joint favorite to repeat as champions next season, level with cross-city rivals Panathinaikos. But while all of the attention is on those two Athens giants, some underdogs are flying under the radar as they prepare to mount their own assault on the summit. 

Žalgiris Kaunas 

Sylvain Francisco finished last season as the runner-up for EuroLeague MVP after leading Žalgiris to a domestic double and a genuine playoff scare against the defending champions — Kaunas pushed Fenerbahçe to four games, the deepest the club has gone in years — and then watched his own signing become a punchline. 

He inked a three-year deal with ASVEL in July. Less than a month later, he was gone, bought out and shipped to Panathinaikos, his name attached to a rumor before the ink on his old contract had dried. That’s the sting nobody in Kaunas saw coming: not losing a player to a rival, but losing him to circumstances entirely outside their control, weeks after he’d been one of the best guards on the continent. 

Žalgiris answered the only way they could, prying Jonas Valančiūnas out of the NBA at 34, hoping a two-time champion’s rim presence outweighs the mileage. It’s domestically that this club never blinks — not a single missed semifinal in its history, another LKL title and King Mindaugas Cup banner this year alone. Europe is the mountain that’s eluded them since the glory years, and this season hinges on whether a reshaped backcourt of Ty Lawson and Duane Washington Jr. can approximate what they just lost.

Red Star Belgrade 

Ibon Navarro’s first walk into the Red Star gym came with seven trophies from four seasons at Unicaja trailing behind him and a very different kind of pressure waiting inside. This is a club with a European title dating to 1974, still measuring itself against a modern era it hasn’t cracked — a play-in exit to Barcelona last season, a Belgrade derby split with Partizan, another season of knocking without the door ever quite giving way. 

Navarro inherits real talent: David Kramer and Nick Weiler-Babb in the backcourt, Johnathan Motley up front, Patrick Baldwin Jr., and a returning Nemanja Nedović. What he doesn’t inherit is patience. Belgrade has watched this roster-and-hope cycle before. Now, the Serbian capital demands results. 

Baskonia 

And then there’s Baskonia, who somehow won a trophy and had a nightmare season in the same year. An 0-6 start bled into a 13-25 finish, out of contention by April, the kind of collapse where you could feel the home crowd going quiet game by game. Then, almost defiantly, they went to Valencia in February and beat Real Madrid 100-89 to win the Copa del Rey, Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot pouring in 28 and Trent Forrest turning in a near triple-double that won him Final MVP. 

Seventh cup in club history. First since 2009. And then the punchline: Luwawu-Cabarrot signed with Real Madrid, the exact team he’d just beaten. Forrest left for Fenerbahçe. The two engines of Baskonia’s only good month are gone, replaced by Chris Duarte, DJ Stewart Jr., Markus Howard, and Kenneth Faried, under a Paolo Galbiati still trying to find out which version of his team shows up in October.

The post Three Potential Sleeper Teams Who Could Upset the EuroLeague Next Season appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama faces political backlash in France over student protest support
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
After backing student protests, Victor Wembanyama enters a different kind of arena

The post Victor Wembanyama faces political backlash in France over student protest support appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Victor Wembanyama is at the center of a political storm in France after politicians criticized the NBA superstar for backing a growing national crisis.

The unrest began as a local high school movement protesting teacher shortages, crowded classrooms, and educational inequality before spreading into nationwide demonstrations.

Wemby himself recently reflected on his own school years in Nanterre, emphasizing that his successful career has not detached him from these struggles. He noted that these deep inequities deserve attention beyond the school gates, and welcomed young people making their voices heard, stating he supports them and hopes authorities do the same.

Friction grew when he shared a cryptic ‘white rabbit’ meme on social media before an October 17 protest. Many fans based in North America initially saw it as excitement for the opener of the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, but conservative officials viewed it as a nod to the unrest.

Les célébrités françaises comme le basketteur Victor Wembanyama qui ont appelé à soutenir les émeutes du 17 octobre portent une responsabilité historique.

Ils doivent être condamnés.

— Eric Ciotti (@eciotti) October 17, 2026

The backlash was led by Eric Ciotti, the right-wing Nice mayor. The 61-year-old politician condemned the two-time All-Star online, arguing that celebrities backing the movement bear a historic responsibility for subsequent riots and deserve formal condemnation. Parliament member Laetitia Ravalet also targeted the player directly, demanding he receive the bill for property damage. Meanwhile, this offensive triggered a defense of the player from various media outlets and cultural figures.

The towering French center has chosen not to answer the attacks, focusing instead on the San Antonio Spurs and the start of official games in his 2026–27 journey. The team coached by Mitch Johnson opens their 82-game schedule against the Oklahoma City Thunder in Frost Bank Center on Tuesday.

item.title: Avdija ready for two-way leap, previews revamped roster: “Rock and roll”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A global Portland Trail Blazers roster prepares to open the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season

The post Avdija ready for two-way leap, previews revamped roster: “Rock and roll” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The Portland Trail Blazers are entering the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season with a completely revamped roster.

In a busy summer, the franchise traded for Ja Morant and hired head coach Micah Nori. Now, they are building a versatile system around its new multi-guard backcourt.

Israeli forward Deni Avdija is a central piece of this fresh lineup. The 25-year-old standout shined in the Preseason, averaging 17.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game. This year, he aims to become an elite two-way presence.

“My plan is to take another step defensively, especially this year,” he mentioned after team practice on Sunday. “I want to be a great two-way player.”

To fit alongside dominant ball-handlers, including Damian Lillard, the former Maccabi Tel Aviv player and All-Star last season is adapting his game. He expects to play ‘a little bit more off the ball’ but remains confident in the group’s collective flexibility.

“We’re very versatile,” he noted. “We have a lot of players that can play multiple positions. They can put pressure on the rim. They can play defense. I feel like everybody’s mind is there, and obviously the coaching staff is going to do the best job they can to put us in great situations. We’re just going to rock and roll with the lineups.”

This rotation will feature heavy international depth, despite Portland waiving Polish Jeremy Sochan. Avdija is projected to start in the frontcourt next to Belgian Toumani Camara. Meanwhile, French Sidy Cissoko and Czech Vít Krejci will provide European flavor off the bench.

The Blazers open the Regular Season at home against the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, then travel to play the Sacramento Kings on Friday.
